A good field of 20 Junior walkers, that is junior in performance, faced the starter and a very interesting race followed, with Gerry Warr and George Beecham battling all the way for first position.

Syd James, who has been walking well this season, carried on the good work and gained his first Club trophy. George Oliver, who had been with Syd up till the last two miles, finished second, with Gerry Warr third.

McMullen lead the field home from Gerry Warr and Ted Smith, and in the match against Surrey W.C. we won with 89 to 126 pts. We also held an 8 x 110 yds. relay, and with several non-sprinters competing we saw a close race with Bob Wolton once again beating Coxon over the final sprint.

We had three runners pass on to the 2nd round of the 220 yds. in Denis Merrett, Ivan Mayers and Basil Walden, but only Merrett progressed further and he was eventually 4th in the final of this event. Gerry Warr was our sole entry in the 2 miles walk and he finished 7th in 15 mins. 27.6 secs.

Gerry Warr was 2nd in the University one mile at Motspur Park on May 7th. Charlie Speechley—like Johnny Walker—still going strong, won the handicap in the Veterans' match at Parliament Hill on May 20th.
Gerry Warr has gone back to rejoin our Southampton-cum-Eastleigh contingent having taken up residence at Southampton, so we hope he will be seeing something of Percy Wright.
We were pleased to see Gerry Warr and Joe Scamell junr. back on the track, they both just missed the seven miles but gave a glimpse of better things to come.

Unfortunately this event always clashes with our own opening 5 miles, but nevertheless a few of the old faithfuls made up a team with Syd James, Charlie Speechley, Gerry Warr, Norman Guilmant and Percy Wright.

We had a good entry of 34 individuals but unfortunately we lost Eric Hall, Syd James, Norman Guilmant and Bill Ferguson and our first man home was Hugh McGreechan in 31st position. Bob Newson 55th, Gerry Warr [illegible]2nd and Len Demmon 63, made up our scoring four who finished 9th in the team race with 201 points.

Bob Newson capably carried out the duties of Captain in the absence of Harry Shields and taking everything into consideration, the "Cads" left the Polytechnic very pleased with themselves. In the Hampshire 10 Percy Wright finished 3rd after a bad last mile, Gerry Warr was 5th and Norman 6th.
